content:
Another week, another streaming service price hike. ESPN announced this week that the monthly fees for ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited will rise simultaneously, and some Disney+ and Hulu bundle plans will also see price increases.

This price hike was discovered by Sports Media Watch through the ESPN support page, and the new fees will take effect on September 17. Details are as follows:

  • ESPN Select monthly fee: US$14 per month (originally US$13 per month)
  • ESPN Select annual fee: US$140 per year (originally US$130 per year)
  • ESPN Unlimited monthly fee: US$32 per month (originally US$30 per month)
  • ESPN Unlimited annual fee: US$320 per year (originally US$300 per year)

The report points out that this is the first price increase for the service since ESPN revamped its streaming strategy last year.

At the same time, some Disney bundle plans have also raised their monthly fees in response to the ESPN streaming price hike.

  • Disney+ (with ads), Hulu (with ads) plus ESPN Select: US$22 per month (originally US$20 per month)
  • Disney+ (no ads), Hulu (no ads) plus ESPN Select: US$33 per month (originally US$30 per month)

As The Verge noted, this price hike also affects the legacy ad-free Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN Select bundle plans that are no longer accepting new customers, with the monthly fee increasing from US$25 to US$28.

The good news is: ESPN Unlimited bundle plans are not affected by this price hike.

Peacock also announced a price hike last week, with increases of up to US$3 per month or US$30 per year. Apple has also recently raised the prices of Apple Music and Apple One.
